Spectral library import

Source: vignettes/articles/spectral-libraries.Rmd
spectral-libraries.Rmd

GCMSprime keeps raw peaks, chemical identifiers and retention-index provenance together. Small libraries can be used in memory. Large libraries are imported in batches into SQLite and queried without loading every spectrum.

library(GCMSprime)
lib <- readMSP("library.msp", backend="sqlite", db_file="library.sqlite")
lib <- openLibrary("library.sqlite")
libraryMetadata(lib, which=1:10)
spectra(lib, which=1:1000, nominal=TRUE, normalize="l2")
retentionIndices(lib, which=1:1000, phase="DB5")

Matrix rows identify mass values and columns identify library spectra. Raw extraction with format="list" preserves the input mass/intensity arrays, including duplicate masses. Sparse extraction sums duplicate masses. Nominal binning and normalization are explicit choices.

Source formats

  • OpenChrom Agilent and Shimadzu MSP exports use the streaming native reader. Repeated Synon and Comments tags and unknown fields remain available with libraryMetadata(lib, raw=TRUE).
  • MoNA provides NIST-compatible MSP exports, including its GC-MS collection. Those exports use readMSP().
  • Golm MSP exports use the same interface. Source-specific annotations remain in the raw metadata; column and index conventions should be verified from the library’s accompanying metadata.
  • GCMS-ID provides predicted spectra and retention indices as CSV archives. After extraction, use readGCMSID("NP-Atlas.csv", backend="sqlite", db_file="NP-Atlas.sqlite"). Their predicted origin is recorded explicitly.

Retention indices and chemical information

Retention indices form a long table. Multiple index values can belong to the same spectrum, with a phase class, raw column annotation, index convention and provenance. DB1, DB5 and DBWAX identify nonpolar, semi-standard nonpolar and polar classes. Unspecified columns retain an unknown class. A zero RI placeholder is omitted from the index table while remaining in the raw source metadata.

Names, CAS numbers, formulae, InChI, InChIKey and supplied SMILES have normalized columns. Repeated synonyms and additional fields are retained. Each source record remains distinct, including multiple spectra or RI predictions for a compound. Supplied SMILES are preserved in their original form.

Storage and scale

SQLite stores indexed metadata, a separate retention-index table and one pair of little-endian float64 peak blobs per spectrum. File-backed objects retain a path and open read-only connections on demand. Imports use transactions and publish the completed file only after parsing succeeds.

A nominal-mass dgCMatrix requires approximately 12q+4(N+1) bytes for q nonzero peaks across N spectra, excluding metadata. For one million spectra with 80 nonzero peaks each this is about 964 MB; a dense matrix with 1,200 mass rows would require about 9.6 GB. SQLite allows raw high-resolution peaks and metadata to remain on disk while matrix blocks are assembled for subsequent analysis.

Library matching and compound identification can build on this storage layer. The import functions expose both raw peaks and normalized sparse blocks for those analyses.

Search recovered spectra

Use RI calibration and spectral search to identify recovered compounds with column-specific RI constraints, Stein–Scott similarity and symmetric multinomial distances.
